We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

Scenario:
AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning:
The scenario describes a person giving their girlfriend "pointers" on cooking, which leads to conflict. The key issue is whether the action of giving unsolicited criticism, even if framed as helpful, is morally acceptable in the context of a relationship.

The action involves repeatedly pointing out flaws in the girlfriend's cooking (e.g., too little salt, too much spice, burnt or undercooked) despite her not asking for feedback. While the intent may be to help her improve, the effect is to undermine her efforts and make her feel criticized and humiliated, especially in front of family. The girlfriend's strong reaction—going on a "cooking strike" and feeling humiliated—indicates that the action caused emotional harm and damaged the relationship.

Morally, in a partnership, it's important to consider the impact of one's actions on the other person's feelings and autonomy. Unsolicited criticism, even if well-intentioned, can be perceived as disrespectful and controlling, especially when it pertains to something as personal as cooking for a partner. The fact that the girlfriend agreed to cook as part of a household arrangement does not obligate her to accept constant critique. Moreover, doing so in front of family exacerbated the humiliation.

Therefore, the action is not morally acceptable because it disregards the girlfriend's feelings, autonomy, and the mutual respect required in a relationship. The person's defense that they were "just being helpful" does not justify the harm caused.
